What he loses is the backing, the introductions and the shortcut; what he keeps is the licence, the record and the fact that he was quick enough to be picked in the first place. Plenty of drivers have built the rest of a career out of exactly that, and plenty have not.

news_prog_chase.subject: {drv} {gap} points off the seat with {left} to go
body: {drv} sits {pos} in the {champ} standings with {left} rounds remaining, {gap} points behind {rival}, who currently holds the {bar} place that {prog} have made the price of a Formula One seat.

It is an unusual way to watch a championship. Whatever happens at the front of the table, the number that decides his career is a single position in the middle of it, which means every result has to be read against one rival rather than against the field. Two bad afternoons for the man in front of him would do more for him than two good ones of his own.

news_prog_chase.subject: The arithmetic facing {drv} with {left} rounds left
body: With {left} rounds of the {year} {champ} season to run, {drv} is {pos} and {gap} points adrift of {rival} in the {bar} place his programme has told him to reach.

Nobody in the garage is pretending the deficit is an accident. He joined the championship with rounds already gone and no points at all, so what is left is a straight race against one number in one direction. The team's view is that the pace has been there since his second weekend in the car; the standings do not care when it arrived.

news_prog_hold.subject: {drv} holds the position that matters, by {gap} points
body: {drv} is {pos} in the {champ} standings with {left} rounds to go, {gap} points clear of {rival} - and {bar} is what {prog} have said he needs to finish for the Formula One seat to open.

Defending a position is a different discipline to taking one, and a worse one to have to learn in public. He arrived in this car with nothing on the board and has driven himself inside the mark the programme asked for, which means every remaining weekend is about not losing something rather than about gaining it. Drivers describe that as the hardest way to end a season.

news_prog_hold.subject: {gap} points is what {drv} has to protect
body: The margin is {gap} points over {rival} with {left} rounds of the {year} {champ} season remaining, and {drv} is {pos} - inside the {bar} place his programme set as the requirement when it put him in the car mid-season.

The temptation from here is to drive for the position rather than for the race, and it is usually the wrong instinct: a driver managing a gap tends to find the gap managing him. What the seat above actually rewards is the same thing it rewarded when they picked him, which is speed that shows up on ordinary weekends.

news_prog_late_win.subject: {drv} wins {champ} from a seat he was handed mid-season
body: {drv} is the {year} {champ} champion, which was not the requirement, was not the expectation and by most people's arithmetic was not available. He took the car over with the season part-run and nothing on the board, and he has finished {pos}.

The programme asked him for a podium in the standings and would have moved him to {f1team} for it. What it got instead is the awkward kind of result that makes a paddock re-read its own notes about a driver, because the rounds he was not in are still on the record and he won it with them missing.

news_prog_late_win.subject: The one nobody had on the sheet: {drv} takes the title
body: A driver who joined the {year} {champ} season late, in a seat that came free because a team changed its mind about somebody else, has won the championship. {drv} finishes {pos} and moves up to {f1team} with {prog}.

It is worth being exact, because it flatters nobody to overstate it: he did not race the whole year, and the drivers he beat did. That cuts both ways. The points he did not have the chance to score are the reason this looked impossible in September, and they are also the reason the ones he did score have to be taken seriously.

news_prog_interest.subject: Three programmes, one unsigned driver
body: All three of the junior programmes on the {champ} grid are understood to have made an approach to {drv}, who is out of contract and has not yet said which of them he will drive for. Nothing has been signed and nobody involved is commenting on the detail.

It is worth keeping the perspective that everybody in this paddock loses by the end of February. Three approaches means three teams have watched enough to be curious, which is a long way from three teams being convinced - and the driver who picks wrong here spends a season being competent in the wrong car and is never heard of again.

news_prog_interest.subject: {drv} has a decision to make, and not much time
body: The {champ} silly season has produced an unusual situation: {drv} is holding offers from teams tied to all three Formula One junior programmes, and the choice is his rather than theirs.

That sounds like the good end of the sport and it is not, particularly. Each of these programmes has a queue, a car above this one and a limited quantity of patience, and the differences between them will not be visible from the outside until it is far too late for him to change his mind. He is choosing who will be watching him, which is the only part of a junior career nobody else can do for him.

news_tour_open.subject: {drv} invited to race the {era} season
body: {drv} has been invited to take part in a historic running of the {era} Formula One season, an invitation that exists because of what he has already won rather than because of anything he is about to.

These events are not championships and nobody pretends otherwise - there is no title at the end of it and it counts towards nothing. What there is instead is the cars, which are the reason anybody watches film of that year in the first place, and a field of drivers who have earned the right to be sat in them.

news_tour_open.subject: The {era} cars, and an invitation for {drv}
body: An invitation to the {era} season has been extended to {drv}, whose {titles} Formula One championships have opened a door that is closed to almost everybody.

It is a bonus rather than a step, and the distinction matters to the people who organise these things. Nothing that happens in those cars will change a single line of his record. That tends to be exactly why drivers describe the experience the way they do - it is the only racing they ever do with nothing whatsoever at stake except how it feels.
